hooks.text: A mystery object from deep space was falling toward Earth.
A three-foot deep-space object was on a collision course.
An incoming killer asteroid turned out to be hollow junk.

title: The mystery Junk that Struck Earth
description: Astronomers tracked a mystery body on a collision course with Earth only to discover it was a piece of forgotten lunar history.

beats.text: A mystery object from deep space was falling toward Earth.
beats.visual: Catalina Sky Survey telescope dome at Mount Lemmon under a night sky, 2015
queries: Catalina Sky Survey telescope Mount Lemmon

beats.text: Astronomers tracked the three-foot body like a killer asteroid.
beats.visual: Illustration of a small metallic object floating in the blackness of deep space, 2015

beats.text: Its massive orbit stretched far beyond the Moon.
beats.visual: Diagram of a highly eccentric Earth orbit extending past the Moon, 2015

beats.text: But density tests proved the object wasn't solid rock.
beats.visual: Abstract data plot showing orbital perturbation due to solar radiation pressure, 2015

beats.text: The incoming object hit the atmosphere at 25,000 miles per hour.
beats.visual: Simulation of a space object heating up during high-speed atmospheric entry, 2015

beats.text: Ground observers missed the fireball because of heavy clouds.
beats.visual: Heavy rain clouds over the Indian Ocean coast of Sri Lanka, 2015
queries: storm clouds over Indian Ocean coast

beats.text: Researchers flew a chartered business jet to film the breakup.
beats.visual: Exterior shot of a Gulfstream G450 business jet in flight above clouds, 2015

beats.text: The fiery mystery was actually a discarded lunar fuel tank.
beats.visual: Artist rendering of a spent rocket stage or fuel tank floating in deep space, 2015

beats.text: This helped them practice for a mystery object falling toward Earth.
beats.visual: Photograph of the WT1190F fireball disintegrating in the daytime sky, 2015

better_than_last: Shortened beats to strictly follow the 14-word maximum while incorporating specific reviewer feedback on the jet and debris identity.
